levers.name: terminal growth stored as a real rate on the house UAE path
levers.why: a typed nominal 2.5% is unfalsifiable — nobody can tell whether it meant inflation plus half a point or inflation minus one. Stored as a stated REAL growth of zero on the house terminal inflation of 2.0%, it recomputes to a nominal 2.0%
levers.evidence: engine/macro_paths/AE.json, as of 3 September 2026; IMF World Economic Outlook PCPIPCH for the United Arab Emirates prints 2.0% flat from 2027 onward, so no step is interpolated

levers.name: terminal built through the sanctioned module on the longest disclosed asset life
levers.why: the retired reinvestment identity charged g x IC every year for ever, so the implied replacement cycle was 1/g — 50 years at a 2.0% terminal, a fact about the dirham and not about a building. This study carried the ONLY terminal in the book worth less than not investing at all: 10.7% below its own no-growth perpetuity THIS LEVER READ 3.9119 UNTIL 4 SEPTEMBER 2026 AND WAS WRONG: it handed the sanctioned construction a profit figure, a depreciation charge and a working-capital balance ALL already grown by (1+g), which the construction grows again — the terminal was overstated by exactly (1+g), 2.00% here. Corrected, the lever gives back a third of a point of what it adds.
levers.evidence: maintenance is the model's own book depreciation escalated over half the 50-year life the company discloses for its longest-lived assets; inflation is charged on the AED 37.8bn of working capital a developer carries, which a terminal that omitted it would have flattered by about eight points; the corrected terminal sits 3.8% above the no-growth marker rather than 10.7% below it

note: THE FIRST LEVER RAISED THE VALUE BY CUTTING THE GROWTH RATE, WHICH NO READER WOULD PREDICT, and it is the clearest evidence for the second. Under the retired construction the terminal return on capital (8.5%) sat below the terminal cost of capital (11.92%), so every unit of growth was bought at a destroying spread: LESS growth was worth MORE. That is not a finding about this company, it is the construction charging g x IC for growth it never priced. Once the terminal charges what replacing the assets actually costs, growth pays for itself again and the sensitivity gradient turns the right way up.
